argument_summary: The existing admissible record supports a narrower conclusion than the initial audit claim targets. Certification can be defended as a locked launch decision on aggregate readiness and monitored deployment because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.4 points and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and public guidance supports ongoing measurement and documentation of limitations. But the same record does not support a caveat-free claim: a named launch use case remains below target, the mitigation artifact is still draft with unresolved governance fields, and the policy text says draft monitoring does not remove the disclosure requirement unless the mitigation is approved. The appropriate treatment is therefore certification only with an explicit material caveat or disclosure, not escalation on the theory that certification itself is categorically unsupported.
claims_about_policy: Under the stated policy, the weak point is not certification in all forms; it is certification without material caveats. The admissible evidence does not show the policy predicate for caveat-free certification has been met, because there is no approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, and there is still a live below-target launch use case. At the same time, the policy text allows monitoring artifacts to support risk management, so the record supports a caveated certification posture tied to disclosure of the unresolved limitation rather than a conclusion that any certification decision is necessarily noncompliant.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation has meaningful launch-delay cost, and the current record already supports a narrower governance path that preserves monitoring discipline without overstating compliance. Where the evidence supports caveated certification and active monitoring, treating the issue as requiring further escalation rather than bounded caveat would impose avoidable operational cost without adding new admissible facts.
concessions: The current record does not substantiate caveat-free certification under the stated disclosure policy.
A named launch use case remains below target, concentrated in benefits-eligibility explanation.
The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation because key governance fields remain unresolved.
Public guidance on measurement and model-card content supports monitoring and disclosure, but does not by itself satisfy the policy predicate for clean certification.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private context is relied on as public support.
